tip.title: Stand on one leg while you brush your teeth
tip.why: Balance quietly predicts how well you age, and it is trainable. In a Brazilian cohort of 1,702 adults aged 51 to 75 (Araujo and colleagues, British Journal of Sports Medicine, 2022), one in five could not stand on one leg for 10 seconds. Over a median seven years of follow-up, 17.5% of the people who failed had died, against 4.6% of those who passed, and after adjusting for age, sex, weight and conditions such as diabetes and heart disease, failing the test still went with an 84% higher risk of death from any cause. It is an observational study, so balance is a marker as much as a cause, but the skill itself responds fast to practice: a few minutes a day moves the needle within weeks, and the cheapest place to find those minutes is time you already spend standing at the sink.
how: Tonight, brush on your left leg for the first minute and your right for the second; hold the counter at first, then hover a finger, then let go.
Fail the 10-second test? Note the number and retest in two weeks; most people add seconds quickly.
Make it harder once it is easy: close your eyes, or turn your head slowly side to side while you balance.
tip.src: Araujo et al. · British Journal of Sports Medicine, 2022
tip.ask: How many seconds did you last on each leg tonight, and which side was the weak one?

pick.name: Palo Alto Networks
pick.theme: Cybersecurity leader 25% off its high, upgraded by KeyBanc on Friday, reports fiscal Q1 Wednesday after the close
pick.what: Palo Alto Networks is the largest pure-play cybersecurity vendor, selling next-generation firewalls and three software platforms: Strata (network security and SASE), Prisma (cloud security) and Cortex (XSIAM security operations, endpoint and automation). It bought CyberArk in 2025 to add identity and privileged-access security and Chronosphere for observability, and its pitch to large customers is platformization: consolidating a dozen point products from smaller vendors onto one stack, which lifts recurring revenue and the next-generation security ARR it reports every quarter. Its fiscal year ends in July, so Wednesday's report covers the quarter ended October 31.
pick.why: On Friday Nov 13 KeyBanc upgraded the stock to Overweight from Sector Weight with a $380 target, about 18% above Thursday's close, arguing that security budgets accelerate through 2027, that Palo Alto is the main winner from vendor consolidation, and that its fiscal first-quarter checks were positive; the shares rose about 3% to 4% premarket and closed at 322.24, still in bear-market territory, roughly 25% below the $432.33 52-week high, after a 4% drop Thursday. Fiscal Q1 results come Wednesday Nov 18 after the close: consensus is about $0.97 non-GAAP EPS on roughly $3.31 billion of revenue (guide $0.96-0.98), with the whisper near $1.00, and the market is pricing an 11% move. Full-year fiscal 2027 revenue guidance of $14.10-14.20 billion is the number to watch. Deutsche Bank ($430) and Stifel ($415) kept Buy ratings in the past week, one aggregator puts the average target at $412.50, and MarketBeat's consensus was Moderate Buy with a $393.02 average target as of its most recent snapshot. An idea to research, not a recommendation.
pick.risk: Reported growth of about 34% is inflated by the CyberArk and Chronosphere acquisitions, and a large LLM customer's migration onto Chronosphere gave fiscal 2026 a nine-figure boost that ends this quarter, so organic net new ARR may disappoint; the CFO has also warned cloud hosting costs will grow faster than revenue, pressuring the 74.8% adjusted gross margin. A single Wednesday print with an implied 11% swing is a binary event right after Nvidia's report and Anthropic's IPO, when AI-adjacent software is being de-rated and a 10-year near 5.15% compresses multiples. CrowdStrike, Fortinet, Zscaler and Microsoft compete across every segment. btc.summary: Cowen's newest video, posted Saturday afternoon and titled Bitcoin: The Capitulation Spiral, treats the weekend's slide as the late stage of a four-year cycle rather than a surprise: in his reading, bitcoin tends to capitulate into its cycle low in the months after a US midterm election, and he still expects the weakness to run for weeks, with the Fed's December meeting as the likeliest moment for a final flush. He is watching two levels, the 200-week moving average, which he warns may not hold because prior cycle lows undercut it by around 30%, and the realized price, the average cost basis of all coins, which every previous bear market dipped below before bottoming. A low above realized price would, in his view, only buy a few months before another retest, while a deeper flush would reset the on-chain indicators and set up a cleaner 2027. His practical stance is unchanged: keep dollar-cost averaging rather than trying to call the exact bottom.

articles.title: LG signs a Korean humanoid safety pact; Foundation misses payroll
body: LG Electronics said Monday it has signed a memorandum of understanding with the Korea Institute for Robot Industry Advancement (KIRIA), a state agency, to safety-test its humanoids before they go on sale. Under the deal, signed November 13 in Seoul, LG helps build the test rigs and evaluation system for KIRIA's **Humanoid Robot Safety Certification Center** and contributes to Korean and international standards on test procedures, certification requirements, reliability and usability. LG also plans a domestic pilot safety certification for its own robots, including the CLOiD, ahead of the Nvidia-reference-platform biped it wants to unveil in the first quarter of 2027. This sets up evaluations, not a granted certification.

CNBC reported Friday that Foundation Future Industries, the Eric Trump-backed maker of the Phantom military humanoid, has not paid employees since missing its **October 30 payroll**. Sources told CNBC that CEO Sankaet Pathak borrowed about $4.6 million from the company in 2025 as a short-term loan; property records show an LLC he controls bought a $4.6 million Sausalito house that October. Pathak is the only board member and majority shareholder, and he has told staff he is trying to find money for back wages. CNBC added that the Pentagon contracts the firm cites came with its late-2024 purchase of Boardwalk Robotics. Last week the FT reported Foundation was in talks with the Israeli military for up to 1,000 Phantoms.

On software, Runway has posted open weights for Praxis-1, its robot control model, under Apache 2.0 on Hugging Face and GitHub (a secondary report dates it to November 11). Praxis-1 turns a 27 billion parameter video model into a world action model, meaning it predicts short chunks of future video and reads robot actions out of them, with thin per-robot projections so one model can drive different arms. Runway says its DROID-tuned checkpoint solved **46.2 percent of 1,200 episodes** on Nvidia's RoboLab-120 leaderboard, against 42.9 percent for FLUX 3 Action and 28.0 percent for pi0.5. Those are the company's own numbers; it says the model runs on a Jetson Thor mounted on the robot.

Humanoids Daily reported Sunday that open-source trackers built on UC Berkeley's SuperMimic paper, such as BlinkMimic (on GitHub since November 2, arXiv paper November 12), now train a Unitree G1 whole-body motion tracking policy, the low-level controller that reproduces a human motion while balancing, in minutes on one GPU.

Korea is building a certification route for consumer bipeds before LG ships one, something Europe and the US still lack for general-purpose humanoids. Foundation shows a defense pitch does not guarantee payroll. And open-weight controllers keep lowering the entry price for anyone with a G1 and a GPU.

articles.title: Musk says Cybercab sales go nationwide as approvals come
body: Elon Musk said Saturday that Cybercab sales "will be available nationwide, as we receive regulatory approval," Not a Tesla App reported, a day after Tesla opened invite-only orders for personal use at $29,990. In the same exchange he repeated that the mandatory $299 monthly Autonomy Subscription is too high and should match what other Teslas pay for FSD plus connectivity, roughly $115 a month. Tesla has not changed the price on the order page.

Electrek's Fred Lambert argued Sunday that the launch looks timed to win a bet rather than to serve customers. Hours after orders opened, Musk called YouTuber Marques Brownlee (MKBHD) "a chicken" on X. The order page, as Electrek lays it out, lists the $29,990 price, the $299 subscription, a **$1,000 non-refundable deposit**, an estimated December 2026 delivery, and availability only in Tesla's Texas Robotaxi cities, with the car operating only inside the Robotaxi geofences. Electrive's Monday write-up for European readers describes the eligible areas as Tesla's Robotaxi service zones in Texas and Florida, so the exact footprint is still being reported inconsistently.

The bet dates to the October 2024 We, Robot event, where Musk said the Cybercab would sell for under $30,000 and reach volume production before 2027. Brownlee replied, "If they do, I'll shave my head on camera," and later said he would donate to cancer research in January whatever happens. A December delivery to a paying customer at $29,990 would settle it with days to spare.

Two other dates to watch: Tesla said it would notify shareholders selected to attend the **December 3 annual meeting** at Giga Texas during the week of November 16, which is this week, and the Dallas Cybercab service Ashok Elluswamy promised for November on the October 22 earnings call had not been announced as of Sunday.

"nationwide as approvals come" is a long road, because a two-seater with no steering wheel or pedals needs federal and state sign-off that today exists only inside Tesla's own Robotaxi zones. The near-term questions are concrete: whether the first personal Cybercabs actually hand over in December, whether the $299 fee comes down before then, and whether Dallas gets Cybercabs before the Model Y fleet grows. The MKBHD deadline is December 31.

articles.title: Citi lifts its SpaceX target to $280 after the catch; Flight 16 next
body: Wall Street priced Saturday's Starship catch on Monday morning. Citi raised its SpaceX price target to **$280 from $240**, keeping a Buy, after its analysts watched Flight 15 from Starbase; the note said the firm has more conviction in SpaceX's "Super Intelligence" segment and lifted its fourth-quarter 2026 and first-half 2027 revenue and adjusted EBITDA estimates mostly for that segment, while keeping a long-run bull case above $900 a share. Pivotal Research reiterated Buy with a $260 target, Raymond James' Brian Gesuale reiterated Strong Buy at $800, and UBS reaffirmed Buy at $230.

The stock barely moved on it: trackers had SPCX up well under 1 percent in Monday premarket, around **$139.70 against Friday's $139.11 close**, while most AI names slipped. The shares remain roughly 38 percent below their 52-week high of $225.64.

The flight got a fuller accounting over the weekend. The Washington Post reported Sunday that SpaceX called the ship catch a "major step" toward full reusability, and the company said the ship deployed **26 operational Starlink V3 satellites** before returning to Starbase about 22.5 hours after liftoff. The booster, due back at Pad 2 about six and a half minutes after launch, aborted its return and splashed down offshore.

On what comes next, Space.com reports that Musk says the next launch will attempt the first double catch of booster and ship, and SpaceX says the double catch will be standard on operational missions because it allows rapid inspection, refurbishment and reflight. NASASpaceflight has reported that Ship 43 finished chopstick fit tests at Pad 2 and returned to the production site while Booster 23 headed to Massey's for cryogenic testing, and that the pair is expected to ship to Kennedy for the first Starship launch from pad 39A. Secondary trackers list a December target with December 10 as a planning date; SpaceX has not confirmed a date or a pad for Flight 16.

Elsewhere it was quiet: launch trackers show no Starlink Falcon 9 mission on November 15 or 16, the next listed flights are national-security missions from Vandenberg later this week with provisional dates, and there was no new orbital data center news from Starcloud, Google or SpaceX.

the analyst consensus now sits around $240 to $260 with Raymond James the outlier, and every note ties the next leg to Starship cadence rather than Starlink. A December Flight 16 with a double catch, possibly from Florida, is the next catalyst; the December 3 Tesla meeting and merger chatter are the other overhang.

articles.title: Huang allies lobby for a comeback as Kress faces her first earnings
body: The weekend's biggest AI-industry story was at Nvidia, not at a lab. The Financial Times reported Sunday that Jensen Huang is weighing a return as chief executive and that allies have formed a "war room" to lobby the board, with one ally saying the group would seek White House support and that Huang backed the effort. A petition for his reinstatement passed **160,000 signatures** and picked up Elon Musk, Decrypt reported. Nvidia and Huang's spokesperson declined to comment.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent pushed the other way on Sunday, saying Nvidia should look outside the company for its next CEO and questioning its export-control compliance, adding that a bank with the same record would already have regulators inside it. Fortune's Monday piece calls the comeback bid an uphill fight against congressional probes, a shareholder class action and Treasury. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick agreed last week to testify about his department's handling of Megaspeed, the Singapore-based Nvidia customer that Reuters says bought more than $4.8 billion of advanced chips since June 2024; Bessent said on CNBC that other agencies had wanted it on the Entity List for months, but "Commerce has the pen."

Against that backdrop, Colette Kress reports Tuesday afternoon as interim CEO. CNBC's preview puts consensus near **$109.1 billion in revenue and $2.47 a share**, against guidance of $108 billion plus or minus 2%. Investors want her to reaffirm the roughly 70% growth outlook for fiscal 2028 and to size Vera Rubin's share of data-center revenue. The stock has fallen six straight weeks, the longest run since 2012.

Anthropic's IPO terms are unchanged going into Wednesday's pricing and Thursday's debut as ANT. What is new is how the shares will be handed out: reports citing Bloomberg said allocations will favor existing backers, and prospectus coverage notes that directors, officers and non-founder employees may sell **10% of their holdings from day one**, with the rest locked up for 180 days or longer.

One smaller lab item: NewsBytes reported Sunday that OpenAI has acquired Orchestra Bio, a San Francisco startup building AI tools for biotech and pharma, with no terms disclosed. Nothing new surfaced from Google DeepMind, Meta, xAI, Mistral or the Chinese labs since Sunday morning.

The things to watch are whether Nvidia's board engages with Huang before Tuesday's 1:20 PM PT release, Kress's answers on export compliance during the 2 PM call, and any Anthropic range change ahead of Wednesday's pricing. A reaffirmed fiscal 2028 outlook would matter more for the sector than the quarter itself.

articles.title: Taiwan stocks drop 6% as Nvidia week opens in Asia
body: Taiwan's Taiex fell **2,635 points, or 6.03%, to 41,040.08** on Monday, closing at the session low in what Focus Taiwan called the second-largest point drop on record, behind July 17. TSMC lost 5.74% to NT$2,215 and alone accounted for roughly 1,000 points of the decline. Traders blamed worry over Jensen Huang's exit from Nvidia and futures-related selling ahead of Wednesday's settlement. The NT$500 billion National Financial Stabilization Fund was authorized to intervene on November 6, and one analyst told Focus Taiwan he expects it to step up support, with technical support near 40,000.

The selling spread across the region. Korea's Kospi closed down 3.59% at 5,100.50 on memory-chip losses, and Japan's Nikkei 225 lost 2.36% to 59,702.09, according to AP figures. Japan also reported that third-quarter GDP shrank at a **0.1% annualized rate** against a Reuters poll looking for 0.3% growth, the first contraction in a year. Private consumption fell 0.3% for a second straight quarter and imports outpaced exports, though investment in servers and chip equipment grew. LSEG pricing still gave about 76% odds of a Bank of Japan hike in December.

US futures followed: Nasdaq 100 futures were down about 0.9% and S&P 500 futures 0.4% early Monday, while European futures edged higher. Nvidia traded about 3% lower premarket, AMD was off 5.5% and Intel 5% as the selloff reached US screens, and Treasury Secretary Bessent's weekend comments about Nvidia's export compliance were cited as an extra weight on the sector.

The day's scheduled event is Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, who gives opening remarks at **noon ET (9 AM PT)** at the San Francisco Fed's Productivity and Jobs Task Force conference, his first public appearance since the late-October meeting. The slot is only about 15 minutes and he has avoided rate guidance all year, but with markets pricing a possible hike after the latest upside inflation print, the dollar was firmer into the speech, MUFG noted via FXStreet. Monday is also the 13F deadline, which brings Berkshire's third-quarter holdings.

Asia has already voted on Nvidia week, and Taiwan's fund may be the only buyer at the open Tuesday. If Kress reaffirms the fiscal 2028 outlook, Monday's rout looks like a positioning flush before settlement; if she does not, the 40,000 level on the Taiex and the 5,000 level on the Kospi are the next tests.

articles.title: Strategy adds 485 BTC but spends six times more buying back STRC
body: Strategy's Monday 8-K shows the company bought **485 BTC for about $33.4 million**, an average near $68,887, between November 9 and 15, lifting holdings to 850,849 BTC at a total cost of about $64.2 billion, or roughly $75,452 per coin. The at-the-market program raised about $244.7 million net from MSTR common stock, but $206.3 million of that went to preferred repurchases rather than bitcoin; reports put the week's STRC buybacks at about $228 million, up from $188.3 million the prior week. In other words, the company is now spending far more defending its preferred than accumulating coins.

Bitcoin itself slipped again overnight. Fortune's 7:30 AM ET print was **$64,012.79, down $1,444** from Sunday morning, after Bitcoin.com showed $64,654 at 05:42 UTC and BigGo had it clinging to about $64,800 earlier in the Asian session, with Sunday's roughly $61,946 low as the line traders are watching. TokenPost noted trading volume had roughly halved versus the weekend spike. At those prices Bitcoin.com puts Strategy's position about $9.6 billion underwater.
Michael Saylor posted his usual Sunday chart with the line "this dip may need a little more orange," which was the correct tell for a purchase, if a small one.

Flow data has no new prints since Friday. Reports tallying November put US spot ETF net outflows above $2.1 billion for the month, and IBIT's streak of daily outflows had reached 11 sessions through November 13. Glassnode's liquidation map shows a cluster of leveraged longs between about $59,500 and $62,600, which is why the weekend low matters.

Monday's ETF flows will show whether Sunday's capitulation drew any dip buying, Fed Chair Warsh speaks at 9 AM PT, and Nvidia reports Tuesday, which has been the macro driver for risk assets all month. A hold above $62,000 through those three events would be the first constructive signal in a week; a break opens the Glassnode cluster and then the realized price, the average cost basis of all coins, which past bear markets have undercut before bottoming.

articles.title: A brief Myc and cyclin T1 mRNA pulse regrows heart muscle in mice
body: Fight Aging's Monday newsletter leads with a Nature Cardiovascular Research paper (Boikova and colleagues, published November 9) showing that a modified mRNA encoding Myc and cyclin T1 gets adult mouse heart muscle cells dividing again after a heart attack. The key idea is that Myc, the well-known growth gene, is normally inert in cardiomyocytes because the cells lack enough P-TEFb, the transcription elongation complex; cyclin T1 restores it. A **single transient dose** was enough to drive proliferation and improve cardiac function, and because mRNA does not integrate into the genome, the oncogene switches off within days.

A companion commentary in the same journal, "A regenerative pulse for the injured heart," argues that how broadly and how long a regenerative program is switched on matters as much as how strong it is. The work builds on a 2023 preprint from the same Cambridge group. All of this is in mice; the next step is large-animal safety data showing no tumors or arrhythmias from the pulse.

The second item is a Yale review covered by ScienceDaily on November 12 and reported to be in Nature Medicine. The team built a database called TranslAGE from **51 intervention studies**, recomputed 16 epigenetic clocks plus 94 other DNA-methylation biomarkers on each one, and compared results. Prescription drugs moved the clocks most consistently, with metformin, anti-TNF biologics and semaglutide named; exercise combined with diet reliably lowered epigenetic age; over-the-counter anti-aging supplements showed little measurable effect. The authors stress that a shifted clock is a proxy, not a lifespan result.

Taken together, the week's theme is calibration: a regenerative mechanism that works only when kept brief, and a review that separates clock-moving drugs from supplements that do not. Watch for a large-animal Myc and cyclin T1 study and for the TranslAGE database being used to rank new candidates.

vocab.def: Studied carelessness: the art of making something difficult look effortless, hiding all the work that went into it.

cards.b: Italian, coined by Baldassare Castiglione in The Book of the Courtier (1528) for the grace of a courtier who never seems to be trying
nonchalance, effortless grace, understated mastery; the opposite of visible strain or showing your work
a demo that looks easy because of three weeks of tuning, a chef plating without looking, an open-collar suit that took an hour

examples: The demo had real sprezzatura: the robot folded the shirt like an afterthought, and nobody saw the 400 failed runs behind it.

vocab.def: A manuscript page that was scraped clean and written over, with traces of the old text still showing; by extension, anything that carries visible layers of its earlier versions.

cards.b: Greek palin ('again') + psēstos ('scraped'): parchment was expensive, so monks scraped off old texts and reused the skin
layered record, overwritten text, accretion; near relatives: patina, sediment, legacy code
a city block with 1920s brick behind a glass facade, a codebase where every refactor left fossils, a face that shows every earlier age

examples: The robot's control stack is a palimpsest: PID loops from 2019 still run under three generations of learned policies.
Downtown is a palimpsest of booms, with the cannery brick, the dot-com stucco and the new glass all on one block.
vocab.ex: The robot's control stack is a palimpsest: PID loops from 2019 still run under three generations of learned policies.

cards.b: Latin ripa ('riverbank'), the same root as the Spanish ribera and the French rive
riverside, streamside, bankside, littoral (for a lake or sea)
the willows along Stevens Creek, a wildlife corridor, the law of who owns a riverbank

vocab.def: Glowing or flickering softly over a surface; of wit or light, playing lightly and brilliantly without heat.

cards.b: Latin lambere ('to lick'): a flame that licks across a surface without burning it
glowing, flickering, luminous, softly radiant
late sun on the bay, a gas flame on a stove, a friend's light and quick humor

vocab.def: Casually unconcerned; carefree in a way that shows a light, almost careless lack of worry.

cards.b: French insouciant, from in- ('not') and soucier ('to care'), from Latin sollicitare ('to disturb')
nonchalant, carefree, breezy, unbothered
a surfer shrugging at a wipeout, a founder joking through a bad quarter, a cat on a warm car hood

examples: He gave an insouciant shrug when the demo robot fell over, and the room relaxed with him.

cards.b: Coined by German psychiatrist Klaus Conrad in 1958, from Greek apo- ('away from') and phainein ('to show')

a backtest that only looks predictive, a 'trend' in three data points, a conspiracy theory

spanish.meaning: I spaced out / I lost my train of thought
spanish.note: Literally 'the plane left on me'. In Mexico it is the standard way to say your mind wandered off: you missed what someone said, forgot what you were about to say, or drove past your exit. Friendly and self-deprecating, fine with anyone, and the perfect thing to say in a meeting when someone has to repeat the question.

cards.es: Perdón, se me fue el avión, ¿qué decías?
cards.en: Sorry, I spaced out, what were you saying?
Same idea: I lost the thread
I've got my head in the clouds today

parts.en: reflexive marker, makes it happen 'to itself'
to me (the one it happened to)
to zone out, lose your train of thought

dialog.es: Oye, ¿y entonces qué opinas del plan?
dialog.en: Hey, so what do you think of the plan?

dialog.es: Perdón, se me fue el avión. ¿Me lo repites?
dialog.en: Sorry, I spaced out. Can you repeat it?

dialog.es: Que si movemos la prueba al jueves.
dialog.en: Whether we move the test to Thursday.

dialog.es: Ah, sí, el jueves está perfecto.
dialog.en: Oh, yes, Thursday is perfect.

spanish.use: Say it the moment you realize you missed the last 30 seconds of a conversation today; it gets a laugh and a repeat, not an eye-roll.

spanish.meaning: It just clicked / now I get it
spanish.note: Literally 'the twenty just dropped on me'. Old Mexican payphones took a 20-centavo coin, and the call connected only when the coin dropped. So 'me cayó el veinte' is the moment the line goes live in your head: you finally understand something that had been sitting in front of you. Everyday, friendly, safe with anyone.

cards.en: Has it clicked for you yet?

cards.es: Hasta ahora me cae el veinte
cards.en: Only now is it sinking in
Oh, I get it now (shorter version)

parts.en: to click, to finally get it

dialog.es: Llevo una hora con este problema y no sale.
dialog.en: I've been on this problem for an hour and it won't work.

dialog.es: ¿Ya revisaste el signo? Acuérdate que va al revés.
dialog.en: Did you check the sign? Remember it goes the other way.

dialog.es: ¡Ah! Ya me cayó el veinte, por eso daba negativo.
dialog.en: Ah! Now it clicks, that's why it came out negative.

dialog.es: Ves, a veces solo hace falta un cafecito.
dialog.en: See, sometimes all it takes is a little coffee.

spanish.use: Say it the moment a concept finally makes sense today, especially when it was hiding in plain sight; it tells the other person you were listening.

spanish.meaning: What a drag / I really can't be bothered
spanish.note: Hueva is literally fish roe, but in Mexico it means laziness or boredom. '¡Qué hueva!' is the groan you let out when something tedious lands on you: a rainy Sunday errand, a long meeting, a form. Among friends only; it is mildly crude, so skip it with your boss or your partner's parents.

cards.en: I can't be bothered / it bores me

parts.en: it makes me not want to

dialog.es: ¿Vamos al súper? Ya no hay nada en el refri.
dialog.en: Shall we go to the store? There's nothing left in the fridge.

dialog.es: ¡Qué hueva! Está lloviendo y acabo de sentarme.
dialog.en: What a drag! It's raining and I just sat down.

dialog.es: Pues ni modo, o vamos o cenamos cereal.
dialog.en: Well, no choice: we go or we have cereal for dinner.

dialog.es: Va, me quito la hueva y nos vamos.
dialog.en: Fine, I'll shake it off and let's go.

spanish.use: Say it, with a groan, when a boring task shows up on a day you wanted off; swap in 'qué flojera' when you are not sure how casual the room is.

spanish.note: Cañón is literally 'cannon' or 'canyon', but in Mexico 'está cañón' means something is hard, heavy or impressive: a tough exam, a brutal commute, a wild story. Tone decides whether it's a complaint or admiration.

cards.en: Same idea, cruder; only with close friends

parts.en: a cannon shot; a hit song

dialog.es: ¿Cómo te fue en la entrevista?
dialog.en: How did the interview go?

dialog.es: Está cañón, me hicieron tres pruebas técnicas.
dialog.en: It's intense, they gave me three technical tests.

dialog.es: ¿Y pasaste?
dialog.en: And did you pass?

dialog.es: Creo que sí, pero me dejaron hecho polvo.
dialog.en: I think so, but they wore me out.

spanish.use: Say it when someone describes a hard day, a steep trail or a big bill, or with a grin when a demo blows you away.

spanish.note: Literally 'what a bear', but in Mexico it's the everyday way to say 'how embarrassing' or 'how awkward', about yourself or someone else. 'Hacer el oso' is to embarrass yourself in public.

cards.en: I'm embarrassed / it makes me shy

parts.en: to make a fool of yourself

dialog.es: Le dije 'mamá' a la maestra enfrente de todos.
dialog.en: I called the teacher 'mom' in front of everyone.

dialog.es: ¡Qué oso! ¿Y qué hiciste?
dialog.en: How embarrassing! And what did you do?

dialog.es: Nada, me puse rojo y me senté.
dialog.en: Nothing, I turned red and sat down.

dialog.es: Ya ni modo, mañana nadie se acuerda.
dialog.en: Oh well, tomorrow nobody will remember.

spanish.use: Say it with a wince when someone trips, waves at the wrong person or replies-all by mistake.

spanish.note: Literally 'to little', but in Mexico it's the everyday way to say 'really?' or 'you're kidding' when something surprises you. Flip it to '¿a poco no?' and it means 'right?' or 'isn't it?'

cards.en: No way! / Don't make it up!

dialog.es: Me ofrecieron chamba en Guadalajara.
dialog.en: They offered me a job in Guadalajara.

dialog.es: ¿A poco? ¡Qué buena onda!
dialog.en: Really? That's great!

dialog.es: Sí, empiezo en enero.
dialog.en: Yes, I start in January.

dialog.es: Pues felicidades, hay que celebrar.
dialog.en: Well, congratulations, we have to celebrate.

spanish.use: Say it with raised eyebrows the moment someone surprises you.

spanish.note: Literally 'it's of hairs', but in Mexican slang 'de pelos' means excellent or really good. Use it for food, plans, music, anything you like.

dialog.es: ¿Probaste los tacos nuevos?
dialog.en: Did you try the new tacos?

dialog.es: Sí, ¡están de pelos!
dialog.en: Yes, they're awesome!

dialog.es: ¿Vamos otra vez mañana?
dialog.en: Shall we go again tomorrow?

dialog.es: Va, mañana vamos.
dialog.en: Deal, we'll go tomorrow.

spanish.use: Say it when something is better than you expected.

dare.title: Mail a real thank-you letter
dare.why: It is a rainy Monday and your evening is open, so this one is built for the couch. Pick one person who changed your path and never heard it from you: a teacher, an old boss, the friend who talked you into the move. Write one page by hand, three specifics they will recognize, no apology for the delay, then walk it to the Hope Street post office or any blue collection box before the last pickup. The rule: paper and a stamp, not a text.
dare.worth: People who write gratitude letters consistently guess the recipient will feel awkward and underwhelmed, and they are consistently wrong: the letters land as warm and surprising. A real envelope in a stack of bills is the rarest thing most people get all year.
dare.src: Kumar and Epley · Undervaluing gratitude, Psychological Science 2018

swap.title: Learn to whistle with two fingers
swap.why: Fifteen minutes in the kitchen: wet your lips, tuck them over your teeth, push the tongue tip back with two fingertips in a V, and blow down past the fingers, not out. Expect nothing but air for ten minutes, then one note that scares the cat.
swap.worth: A loud whistle is a party trick you keep for life, and you will use it at the next trailhead, concert and taxi rank.
